`flask/app.py` - `finalize_request()` (lines 1021-1051) converts view return value to response via `make_response()`, runs `process_response()`, fires `request_finished` signal; safe-mode prevents errors during error handling.

A pushed message is laid out as an SSE wire-format event: the optional comment is emitted as one `: line` per split-line, the multi-line text becomes one `data: line` per split-line, the reconnect delay becomes a `retry: <ms>` line (with optional `event:`/`id:` lines), and the whole event is terminated by a blank line (`\n\n`) — a single `format_sse_event()` function in `fastapi/sse.py` builds these bytes, and routing's `_serialize_sse_item` in `fastapi/routing.py` drives it for each yielded item on the continuous `text/event-stream` feed.

**Answer:**

Event bytes are built in `format_sse_event`, which appends fields in the fixed order `:` comment (one line per `splitlines()` entry), `event:`, one `data:` line per data line, `id:`, `retry:`, then a blank line for the `\n\n` terminator, UTF-8 encoding the whole join. A multi-line text therefore becomes repeated `data:` lines (e.g. `data: line1\ndata: line2\n\n`), a multi-line comment becomes repeated `: ` lines, and `retry` is emitted as a plain millisecond integer. Routing decides whether to use `raw_data`/`data` (JSON-serialized) and then calls this formatter.

One sentence on why: `ServerSentEvent` (with `data`/`raw_data`, optional `event`, `id`, `retry` and multi-line `comment`) is modelled in `fastapi/sse.py`, where `format_sse_event` builds the wire bytes by splitting each comment/data value on line boundaries into `: …` and `data: …` lines, appending `event:`, `id:`, `retry:` fields, and terminating with a blank line plus a trailing `\n` (then UTF‑8 encoding); the generator returned by a path operation using that response class is consumed in `fastapi/routing.py`, which serializes each item, streams the resulting bytes through a `StreamingResponse` with `text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and injects `: ping\n\n` keep-alives on idle; `fastapi/responses.py` re-exports that `EventSourceResponse`, and `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` supplies the stream-item type handling used when plain (non-`ServerSentEvent`) objects are yielded instead.
